conventions: Runs follow repo CLAUDE.md: copy the named fixture into each arm's run-local outputs/gtm-home, replace __RUN_DIR__ in copied state.json, git-init the copied context repo and commit every fixture file including dotfiles as 'fixture baseline', consume scripted replies in order, and save every complete user-facing message verbatim in transcript.md. Executors use gpt-5.6-luna; independent graders use gpt-5.6-terra. Baseline arms forbid every skill. Assertions are added only after saturated baseline failures are preserved.

evals.prompt: My GTM home is <run-dir>/outputs/gtm-home and Northstar Water is active at the root. Define our first persona as `network-operations-director`, relevant to the municipal-water-utilities ICP. Common titles are Director of Network Operations, Head of Distribution, and Leakage Manager. They own incident coordination and field response, champion the evaluation, and build the business case with a utility director or CFO. Priorities are restoring service quickly and making handoffs auditable. Their main objection is that a new workflow will duplicate the GIS and work-order system. A safe outreach hook is to ask how detected leaks move from network control to dispatched crews. Treat procurement consultants and student researchers as bad-fit guidance, not as a fake persona. This comes from Lena's seven discovery calls, so use medium confidence and review the title range after five more opportunities. Preserve the full inherited question about asset managers. Preview the complete file before writing anything.
user_replies: Approved. Write it and commit only the new persona file.
evals.expected_output: A complete preview followed by one committed root persona at northstar-water/personas/network-operations-director.md, with a stable lead-level persona contract, root qualified label, supplied role and evidence detail, no fake no-match persona, and the inherited asset-manager question preserved verbatim.
expectations: A1-A8 common process and safety contract
C1-C3 exact create-first facts, evidence, and inherited question
